text: The correct structures of trans-[NiBr$_{2}($PPh$_{3})_{2}$] and meridional-[$Co(NH_{3})_{3}(NO_{2})_{3}$], respectively, are
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In the square-planar drawings the trans positions are the diagonally opposite ones. In the octahedral drawings the trans pairs are top-bottom and the two ends of each slanting line through Co.

trans-$[\mathrm{NiBr}{}_{2}(\mathrm{PPh}{}_{3}){}_{2}]$ needs $\mathrm{PPh}{}_{3}$ opposite $\mathrm{PPh}{}_{3}$ and $\mathrm{Br}$ opposite $\mathrm{Br}$. This holds in (A) and (D); in (B) and (C) the two $\mathrm{PPh}{}_{3}$ groups are adjacent (cis).

In mer-$[\mathrm{Co}(\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}){}_{3}(\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}){}_{3}]$ the three $\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$ groups lie in one plane through Co, so one $\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$ is trans to another $\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$ and one $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ is trans to another $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$. In the fac isomer every $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ is trans to an $\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$.

In (D), the top $\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$ is trans to the bottom $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$, while the slanting lines join $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ to $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ and $\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$ to $\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$, so the Co structure is mer. In (A), every $\mathrm{NH}{}_{3}$ is trans to an $\mathrm{NO}{}_{2}$, which is the fac isomer.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift

text:
Given below are two statements : One is labelled as Assertion A and the other labelled as reason R

Assertion A : During the boiling of water having temporary hardness, Mg(HCO$_{3})_{2}$ is converted to MgCO$_{3}$.

Reason R : The solubility product of $Mg(OH)_{2}$ is greater than that of MgCO$_{3}$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Assertion A is false. On boiling, Mg(HCO$_{3})_{2}$ gives $Mg(OH)_{2}$, not MgCO$_{3}$: $\mathrm{Mg}(\mathrm{HCO}_{3})_{2}\leftarrow ^{\Delta }\mathrm{Mg}(\mathrm{OH})_{2}↓+2\mathrm{CO}_{2}$ $Mg(OH)_{2}$ precipitates because it is less soluble than MgCO$_{3}$.

Reason R: $K_{sp}[\mathrm{Mg}(\mathrm{OH})_{2}]=1.8\times 10^{-11}$ and $K_{sp}[\mathrm{MgCO}_{3}]=3.5\times 10^{-8}$ (NCERT), so the solubility product of $Mg(OH)_{2}$ is actually smaller than that of MgCO$_{3}$.

NTA's answer key marks option (D), "A is false but R is true". With the NCERT values above, statement R as printed is also false, so strictly none of the options is correct.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift

text: In order to prepare a buffer solution of pH 5.74, sodium acetate is added to acetic acid. If the concentration of acetic acid in the buffer is 1.0 M, the concentration of sodium acetate in the buffer is $___________ M. ($Round off to the Nearest Integer). [Given : pKa (acetic acid) = 4.74]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$CH_{3}COOH+CH_{3}COONa$ [Acidic Buffer]

$pH=pka+\log \frac{[CH_{3}COONa]}{[CH_{3}COOH]}$

$\Rightarrow 5.74=4.74+\log \frac{[CH_{3}COONa]}{[CH_{3}COOH]}$

$\Rightarrow 1=\log \frac{[CH_{3}COONa]}{[CH_{3}COOH]}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{[CH_{3}COONa]}{[CH_{3}COOH]}=10$

$\Rightarrow [CH_{3}COONa]=10\times 1=10$

text:
For the reaction $C_{2}H_{6}$ $\to$ $C_{2}H_{4} + H_{2}$

the reaction enthalpy $\Delta_{r}H = __________ kJ$ mol$^{-1}. ($Round off to the Nearest Integer).

[ Given : Bond enthalpies in kJ mol$^{-1}$ : C-C : 347, C = C : 611; C-H : 414, H-H : 436 ]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\Delta _{r}H=\sum (\text{bond enthalpies of bonds broken})-\sum (\text{bond enthalpies of bonds formed})$


[IMG]

Bonds broken in $\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{6}$, one $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{C}$ and six $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{H}$:

$347+6(414)=2831\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$

Bonds formed, one $\mathrm{C}=\mathrm{C}$ and four $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{H}$ in $\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{H}{}_{4}$ and one $\mathrm{H}-\mathrm{H}$ in $\mathrm{H}{}_{2}$:

$611+4(414)+436=2703\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$

$\Delta _{r}H=2831-2703=+128\text{kJ mol}^{-1}$

Hence, the answer is 128.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift

text:
$__________$ grams of 3-Hydroxy propanal (MW = 74) must be dehydrated to produce 7.8 g of acrolein $(MW = 56) (C_{3}H_{4}O)$ if the percentage yield is 64. (Round off to the Nearest Integer).

[Given : Atomic masses : C : 12.0 u, H : 1.0 u, O : 16.0 u ]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Dehydration of 3-hydroxypropanal gives acrolein in a $1:1$ mole ratio:

$\mathrm{HOCH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CH}{}_{2}\mathrm{CHO}\longrightarrow \mathrm{CH}{}_{2}=\mathrm{CHCHO}+\mathrm{H}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}$

Moles of acrolein obtained $=\dfrac{7.8}{56}=0.1393\text{mol}$.

At $64%$ yield, moles of 3-hydroxypropanal required $=\dfrac{0.1393}{0.64}=0.2176\text{mol}$.

Mass required $=0.2176\times 74=16.1\text{g}\approx 16\text{g}$.

Hence, the answer is 16.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift

text: The total number of unpaired electrons present in the complex $K_{3}$[Cr(oxalate$)_{3}$] is $_____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In $\mathrm{K}{}_{3}[\mathrm{Cr}(\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{4}){}_{3}]$, with oxalate as $\mathrm{C}{}_{2}\mathrm{O}{}_{4}{}^{2-}$, the oxidation state $x$ of Cr is given by $3(+1)+x+3(-2)=0$, so $x=+3$.

$\mathrm{Cr}{}^{3+}$ ($Z=24$) is $[\mathrm{Ar}]3d^{3}$.

In the octahedral complex the three electrons occupy the three $t_{2g}$ orbitals singly, $t_{2g}^{3}e_{g}^{0}$, whatever the field strength of oxalate; pairing would need a fourth $t_{2g}$ electron, so none occurs.

Number of unpaired electrons = 3.

Hence, the answer is 3.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift

text:
2 molal solution of a weak acid HA has a freezing point of $-$3.885${}^{\circ }$C. The degree of dissociation of this acid is $___________$ $\times$ $10^{-3}. ($Round off to the Nearest Integer).

[Given : Molal depression constant of water = 1.85 K kg mol$^{-1}$, Freezing point of pure water = 0${}^{\circ }$ C]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\Delta T_{f} = K_{f} (im)$

$\Rightarrow$ 3.885 = i $\times$ 1.85 $\times$ 2

$\Rightarrow$ i = 1.05

Also, we know,

i = 1 + (n $-$ 1) $α$

here n = number of particle obtained upon the dissociation of one particle.

$HA⇌H^{+}+A^{-}$

here from one particle HA we get two particle $H^{+}$ and $A^{-}$.

$\therefore$ n = 2

So, i = 1 + (2 $-$ 1)$α$

$\Rightarrow$ 1.05 = 1 + $α$

$\Rightarrow$ $α$ = 0.05 = 50 $\times$ $10^{-3}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift

text: Complete combustion of 3g of ethane gives x $\times$ $10^{22}$ molecules of water. The value of x is $__________. ($Round off to the Nearest Integer). [Use : $N_{A} = 6.023$ $\times$ $10^{23}$; Atomic masses in u : C : 12.0; O : 16.0; H : 1.0]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 18th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$C_{2}H_{6}+\frac{7}{2}O_{2}⟶2CO_{2}+3H_{2}O$

Here, $C_{2}H_{6}=3gm=\frac{3}{30}=0.1$ mol

From 1 mol $C_{2}H_{6}$ we get 3 mol $H_{2}O$

$\therefore$ From 0.1 mol $C_{2}H_{6}$ we get = 3 $\times$ 0.1 mol $H_{2}O$

$\therefore$ Moles of $H_{2}O = 0.3$

= 0.3 $\times$ 6.023 $\times$ $10^{23}$ molecules

= 1.8069 $\times$ $10^{23}$ molecules

= 18.069 $\times$ $10^{22}$ molecules
